findings.body:
**Prevent `GH_REPO` from overriding the bound repository.**

At `src/adapters/forge-github/ghEffects.ts:118`, the child inherits `GH_REPO`. GitHub CLI uses this variable to select the repository instead of the local checkout. ([cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_environment?utm_source=openai))

For example, bind the adapter to `/work/target` while `GH_REPO=other/repo`. `editPrBody(123, body)` then replaces the body of PR 123 in `other/repo`, if authorized. Setting `cwd` does not preserve the adapter's repository binding.

Remove the inherited repository override from the child environment, or explicitly select the repository derived from `repoRoot`.
findings.title: Prevent `GHREPO` from overriding the bound repository.

findings.body:
**Reject a readiness snapshot when the PR head changes during the read.**

`getPrReadiness` gets checks from one `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` call (`src/adapters/forge-github/ghEffects.ts:517-524`). In gh v2.65.0, when the fields include `statusCheckRollup`, `Find` runs `preloadPrChecks` to fetch check contexts past the first page. Each extra query reads the PR's current first commit node (`Nodes[0]`) and appends its contexts. The loop never compares the commit OID with the head that produced the first page. If the head changes between pages, the cursor from the old head can append contexts from the new head. The combined rollup can then mix two heads, and `readinessSnapshotOf` (`ghEffects.ts:385-398`) receives no head identity to detect the mix. A mixed rollup can report `pass` while the current head has failing checks on a page that was never appended.

Do not pin pages to one head by changing the query. Instead, read `headRefOid` before and after the `gh pr view` call. Return an error when the two values differ, so the caller does not use the snapshot.
findings.title: Reject a readiness snapshot when the PR head changes during the read.
